{
  "title": "Action Plans for Key Central Texas Education, Child Care, and Disability Resources",
  "summary": "Step‑by‑step, plain‑language action plans to help a Goodwill Workforce Advancement client apply for child care help, GED/ESL and diploma programs, youth training with stipends, and disability-related supports in Central Texas.",
  "content": "### Workforce Solutions Capital Area – Child Care Services
**How to apply:**
- Go to the parent application page: https://wfscapitalarea.com/our-services/childcare/for-parents/ and click **“Apply for Child Care Assistance”** to reach the TX3C site.
- Create or log in to your **Texas Child Care Connection (TX3C)** account, then complete the **Eligibility Screener & Waitlist Application**.
- If you need help, call **512-597-7191** or visit a Career Center at **9001 N IH 35 #110** or **3401 Webberville Rd, Bldg 1000, Austin** during weekday business hours.

**Documents needed:**
- Photo ID for the parent (driver’s license, state ID, or other valid ID)
- Proof you live in Travis County (lease, utility bill, or mail with your name and address)
- Proof of work, job search, or school/training (pay stubs, work schedule, school/training schedule)
- Proof of household income (recent pay stubs, award letters, or other income records)

**Timeline:**
- Waitlist plus review can take **several weeks to a few months**, depending on funding.

**Key tip:**
- Complete the **online waitlist form as soon as possible**, since spots are given in order and funding is limited.

---

### ACC Adult Education – GED / HSE & ESL
**How to apply:**
- Go to https://adulted.austincc.edu and choose **GED / High School Equivalency** or **English as a Second Language (ESL)**.
- For ESL, click the **“Join Interest List”** button on the ESL page and follow the steps to create an account and add your name.
- For GED/HSE, use the Adult Ed site to fill out the **online application/interest form**, or call **512-223-5123** for help and testing dates.

**Documents needed:**
- Valid photo ID (Texas ID, driver’s license, passport, or similar)
- Proof you live in the ACC service area (Travis or nearby county address)
- If age 17–18, parent consent form and high school withdrawal form (if last school was in Texas)
- Any immigration status documents if requested (for eligibility checks)

**Timeline:**
- **1–4 weeks** from interest list to class start, depending on session dates and space.

**Key tip:**
- After you join the interest list, **check your email often** so you don’t miss your testing and registration appointment.

---

### Literacy Coalition of Central Texas – GED & Adult Education
**How to apply:**
- Go to the “Future Students” page: https://literacyctx.org/future-students/ and click **“Get Started”** or the **Student Interest Form** link.
- Complete the online **Student Interest Form** with your contact information and what classes you want (GED, basic education, etc.).
- Answer calls, texts, or emails from staff to finish enrollment and pick your class (online or in-person).

**Documents needed:**
- Photo ID (for example, state ID, driver’s license, or passport)
- Basic contact information and where you live (Travis or nearby county)
- Income and household information if they check eligibility for free classes
- Any previous school or test records, if you have them (helpful but usually not required)

**Timeline:**
- Often **2–4 weeks** from interest form to starting a class, depending on openings.

**Key tip:**
- Fill out the **interest form fully and clearly**, because staff use it to place you and contact you for the next open class.

---

### Goodwill Excel Center (Adult High School Diploma)
**How to apply:**
- Go to the main enrollment site: https://excelcenterhighschool.org/enroll-now/ and choose the **Austin (Norwood Park Blvd)** campus.
- Complete the **online enrollment form** with your contact info, past schools, and education history.
- Watch for a call or email from Excel Center staff to schedule an **intake/registration appointment** at **1015 Norwood Park Blvd, Austin, TX 78753**.

**Documents needed:**
- Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or other valid ID)
- Any high school transcripts or records you have (from all schools you attended)
- Proof of address (recent mail, lease, or utility bill)
- If under 19, parent/guardian information and any required consent forms

**Timeline:**
- **2–6 weeks** from online form to starting classes, depending on term dates and space.

**Key tip:**
- Bring **all past school records** you can find; this can give you more transfer credits and help you finish faster.

---

### American YouthWorks – YouthBuild Austin
**How to apply:**
- Go to the YouthBuild page: https://americanyouthworks.org/what-we-do/youthbuild and click the **Interest Form** or **Apply** link.
- Fill out the **online interest form** with your age, school history, and contact info.
- Answer calls/texts from a YouthBuild recruiter and attend an **information/interview session** at **1901 E Ben White Blvd, Austin, TX 78741**.

**Documents needed:**
- Photo ID (or school ID if that is what you have)
- Social Security card or work-authorization document, if available
- Past school records or withdrawal papers (to show you are out of school and need GED/diploma)
- Proof of income or public benefits for your household, if requested

**Timeline:**
- **2–8 weeks**, depending on when the next YouthBuild cohort starts.

**Key tip:**
- Reply quickly to calls and texts from staff; **spots are limited**, and fast follow-up helps you secure a place in the next group.

---

### Easterseals Central Texas – Disability Services
**How to apply:**
- Go to https://www.easterseals.com/centraltx/ and click **“Contact Us”** or **“Programs & Services”** to choose the service that fits you (employment, therapy, parent support, etc.).
- Call **512-615-6800** and ask for **intake for disability services**; request an appointment or referral instructions.
- Complete any intake forms they send you (online or paper) and attend the intake appointment at **8505 Cross Park Dr, Suite 120, or current main office listed on their site**.

**Documents needed:**
- Photo ID for you or your child’s parent/guardian
- Any medical, school, or evaluation records that show the disability or delay
- Insurance or Medicaid card, if you have one
- Proof of address and income, if they check for sliding-scale or grant-funded services

**Timeline:**
- **A few weeks to a few months**, depending on the specific program and waitlists.

**Key tip:**
- When you call, **ask about all programs you might qualify for** (therapy, employment help, parent support), so you get on every waitlist that fits your needs.

---

### Bluebonnet Trails Community Services – IDD & Behavioral Health
**How to apply:**
- Go to https://bbtrails.org and click **“Contact”** or **“Services”** to find IDD or mental health intake information.
- For new routine services, call the **appointments line: 844-309-6385** and ask for **intake** in your county.
- For a crisis, call the **24/7 crisis hotline: 800-841-1255** right away.

**Documents needed:**
- Photo ID
- Proof of residence in a county they serve (for example, Williamson, Bastrop, Burnet, Caldwell, Fayette, Gonzales, Guadalupe, Lee)
- Insurance, Medicaid/Medicare card, or income information (they serve people with and without insurance)
- Any past mental health or disability evaluations, if you have them

**Timeline:**
- Crisis help is **same day** by phone; non‑emergency intakes are often **1–4 weeks**, depending on demand.

**Key tip:**
- When you call, **say clearly if it is an emergency or non‑emergency**, so they can route you to the right team quickly.

---

### Texas Health and Human Services – Child Care Regulation & Disability Supports
**How to apply (child care search & checks):**
- Go to the child care search page from HHS: from https://www.hhs.texas.gov click **“Services” → “Children” → “Child Care”** and use the link to the **Texas Child Care Search / Availability Portal** to look up licensed providers near you.
- Use the search filters to check **which providers are licensed and if they take subsidy**.
- For general help, dial **2-1-1** and ask for **help finding licensed child care** in your area.

**How to explore disability-related supports:**
- On https://www.hhs.texas.gov click **“Services” → “Disability”** to read about Medicaid waivers, attendant care, and long-term services.
- Call **2-1-1** and ask to be connected to **Texas HHS disability services** to learn which programs you might qualify for.

**Documents needed (varies by program):**
- For child care search only: no documents needed to look up licensed providers online.
- For disability services applications: photo ID, proof of Texas residence, income information, and medical or psychological records showing the disability.
- For Medicaid waiver or long-term care: Social Security number and insurance/Medicaid details, if you have them.

**Timeline:**
- **Right away** for child care search; **months or longer** for many disability and Medicaid waiver programs.

**Key tip:**
- For disability supports, **call 2-1-1 early** and ask about waitlists (like Medicaid waivers) so you can get on the list as soon as possible, even if services start later."
